1.text: A strange seed was planted on its back at birth. The plant sprouts and grows with this Pokémon.
While it is young, it uses the nutrients that are stored in the seeds on its back in order to grow.
It can go for days without eating a single morsel. In the bulb on its back, it stores energy.
For some time after its birth, it grows by gaining nourishment from the seed on its back.

2.text: When the bulb on its back grows large, it appears to lose the ability to stand on its hind legs.
Exposure to sunlight adds to its strength. Sunlight also makes the bud on its back grow larger.
When the bud on its back starts swelling, a sweet aroma wafts to indicate the flower’s coming bloom.
The bulb on its back grows as it absorbs nutrients. The bulb gives off a pleasant aroma when it blooms.

3.text: The plant blooms when it is absorbing solar energy. It stays on the move to seek sunlight.
A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.
By spreading the broad petals of its flower and catching the sun’s rays, it fills its body with power.
After a rainy day, the flower on its back smells stronger. The scent attracts other Pokémon.

4.text: Obviously prefers hot places. When it rains, steam is said to spout from the tip of its tail.
If it's healthy, the flame on the tip of its tail will burn vigorously, even if it gets a bit wet.
The flame at the tip of its tail makes a sound as it burns. You can only hear it in quiet places.
The flame on its tail shows the strength of its life force. If it is weak, the flame also burns weakly.

5.text: When it swings its burning tail, it elevates the temperature to unbearably high levels.
Tough fights could excite this Pokémon. When excited, it may blow out bluish- white flames.
It is very hotheaded by nature, so it constantly seeks opponents. It calms down only when it wins.
If it becomes agitated during battle, it spouts intense flames, incinerating its surroundings.

6.text: Spits fire that is hot enough to melt boulders. Known to cause forest fires unintentionally.
When this Pokémon expels a blast of superhot fire, the red flame at the tip of its tail burns more intensely.
Breathing intense, hot flames, it can melt almost anything. Its breath inflicts terrible pain on enemies.
It uses its wings to fly high. The temperature of its fire increases as it gains experience in battle.

7.text: After birth, its back swells and hardens into a shell. Powerfully sprays foam from its mouth.
The shell is soft when it is born. It soon becomes so resilient, prodding fingers will bounce off it.
It shelters itself in its shell, then strikes back with spouts of water at every opportunity.
When it retracts its long neck into its shell, it squirts out water with vigorous force.

8.text: Often hides in water to stalk unwary prey. For swimming fast, it moves its ears to maintain balance.
This Pokémon is very popular as a pet. Its fur-covered tail is a symbol of its longevity.
When tapped on its head, this Pokémon will pull it in, but its tail will still stick out a little bit.
Its large tail is covered with rich, thick fur that deepens in color with age. The scratches on its shell are evidence of this Pokémon’s toughness in battle.

9.text: A brutal Pokémon with pressurized water jets on its shell. They are used for high speed tackles.
It crushes its foe under its heavy body to cause fainting. In a pinch, it will withdraw inside its shell.
It deliberately makes itself heavy so it can withstand the recoil of the water jets it fires.
Once it takes aim at its enemy, it blasts out water with even more force than a fire hose.

10.text: Its short feet are tipped with suction pads that enable it to tirelessly climb slopes and walls.
When attacked by bird Pokémon, it resists by releasing a terrifically strong odor from its antennae, but it often becomes their prey.
Perhaps because it would like to grow up quickly, it has a voracious appetite, eating a hundred leaves a day.
If you touch the feeler on top of its head, it will release a horrible stink to protect itself.

11.text: This Pokémon is vulnerable to attack while its shell is soft, exposing its weak and tender body.
Its hard shell doesn’t crack a bit even if Pikipek pecks at it, but it will tip over, spilling out its insides.
Its shell is filled with a thick liquid. All of the cells throughout its body are being rebuilt in preparation for evolution.
It is waiting for the moment to evolve. At this stage, it can only harden, so it remains motionless to avoid attack.

12.text: In battle, it flaps its wings at high speed to release highly toxic dust into the air.
Close examination of its large eyes reveals that each eye is composed of a myriad of tiny eyes.
It has a superior ability to search for delicious honey from flowers. It can seek, extract, and carry honey from flowers blooming over six miles away.
When attacked by other Pokémon, it defends itself by scattering its poisonous scales and fluttering its wings.

13.text: Often found in forests, eating leaves. It has a sharp venomous stinger on its head.
Its poison stinger is very powerful. Its bright-colored body is intended to warn off its enemies.
The barb on top of its head secretes a strong poison. It uses this toxic barb to protect itself.
It eats its weight in leaves every day. It fends off attackers with the needle on its head.

14.text: Almost incapable of moving, this Pokémon can only harden its shell to protect itself from predators.
Although it is a cocoon, it can move a little. It can extend its poison barb if it is attacked.
Nearly incapable of movement, it leans against stout trees while waiting for its evolution.
From this form, it will grow into an adult. As its body becomes softer, the external shell hardens.

15.text: Flies at high speed and attacks using its large venomous stingers on its forelegs and tail.
It uses sharp, poisonous stings to defeat prey, then takes the victim back to its nest for food.
It can take down any opponent with its powerful poison stingers. It sometimes attacks in swarms.
May appear in a swarm. Flies at violent speeds, all the while stabbing with the toxic stinger on its rear.

16.text: A common sight in forests and woods. It flaps its wings at ground level to kick up blinding sand.
It has an extremely sharp sense of direction. It can unerringly return home to its nest, however far it may be removed from its familiar surroundings.
Does not like to fight. It hides in tall grass and so on, foraging for food such as small bugs.
It is docile and prefers to avoid conflict. If disturbed, however, it can ferociously strike back.

17.text: Very protective of its sprawling territorial area, this Pokémon will fiercely peck at any intruder.
It slowly flies in a circular pattern, all the while keeping a sharp lookout for prey.
The claws on its feet are well developed. It can carry prey such as an Exeggcute to its nest over 60 miles away.
This Pokémon flies around, patrolling its large territory. If its living space is violated, it shows no mercy in thoroughly punishing the foe with its sharp claws.

18.text: When hunting, it skims the surface of water at high speed to pick off unwary prey such as Magikarp.
Its well-developed chest muscles make it strong enough to whip up a gusty windstorm with just a few flaps.
This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.
Its outstanding vision allows it to spot splashing MAGIKARP, even while flying at 3300 feet.

19.text: Bites anything when it attacks. Small and very quick, it is a common sight in many places.
It searches for food all day. It gnaws on hard objects to wear down its fangs, which grow constantly during its lifetime.
With their strong capacity for survival, they can live in dirty places without concern. Left unchecked, their numbers multiply rapidly.
This Pokémon is common but hazardous. Its sharp incisors can easily cut right through hard wood.

20.text: It uses its whiskers to maintain its balance. It apparently slows down if they are cut off.
With its long fangs, this surprisingly violent Pokémon can gnaw away even thick concrete with ease.
People say that it fled from its enemies by using its small webbed hind feet to swim from island to island in Alola.
It whittles its constantly growing fangs by gnawing on hard things. It can chew apart cinder walls.

21.text: Eats bugs in grassy areas. It has to flap its short wings at high speed to stay airborne.
It busily flits around here and there. Even if it is frail, it can be a tough foe that uses MIRROR MOVE.
Its reckless nature leads it to stand up to others—even large Pokémon—if it has to protect its territory.
It flaps its short wings to flush out insects from tall grass. It then plucks them with its stubby beak.

22.text: With its huge and magnificent wings, it can keep aloft without ever having to land for rest.
A Pokémon that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.
It shoots itself suddenly high into the sky, then plummets down in one fell swoop to strike its prey.
It’s tough and has excellent stamina. It has no problem flying continuously for a whole day carrying a heavy load.

23.text: Moves silently and stealthily. Eats the eggs of birds, such as PIDGEY and SPEAROW, whole.
It always hides in grass. When first born, it has no poison, so its bite is painful, but harmless.
By dislocating its jaw, it can swallow prey larger than itself. After a meal, it curls up and rests.
The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.

24.text: It is rumored that the ferocious warning markings on its belly differ from area to area.
This Pokémon has a terrifically strong constricting power. It can even flatten steel oil drums. Once it wraps its body around its foe, escaping is impossible.
With a very vengeful nature, it won’t give up the chase, no matter how far, once it targets its prey.
To intimidate foes, it spreads its chest wide and makes eerie sounds by expelling air from its mouth.

25.text: When several of these Pokémon gather, their electricity could build and cause lightning storms.
It keeps its tail raised to monitor its surroundings. If you yank its tail, it will try to bite you.
Possesses cheek sacs in which it stores electricity. This clever forest-dweller roasts tough berries with an electric shock before consuming them.
When it is angered, it immediately discharges the energy stored in the pouches in its cheeks.

26.text: Its long tail serves as a ground to protect itself from its own high-voltage power.
It unleashes electric shocks that can reach 100,000 volts. When agitated, it can knock out even an Indian elephant.
Because so many Trainers like the way Pikachu looks, you don’t see this Pokémon very often.
If the electric pouches in its cheeks become fully charged, both ears will stand straight up.

27.text: Burrows deep underground in arid locations far from water. It only emerges to hunt for food.
It can roll its body into a ball. It moves through the desert by rolling at high speeds.
It prefers dry, sandy places because it uses the sand to protect itself when threatened.
When its skin gets wrinkled from moisture, it heads for a volcano. It lies flat on a spot with a lot of geothermal heat and dries itself out.

28.text: Curls up into a spiny ball when threatened. It can roll while curled up to attack or escape.
Although they are sharp, its claws and spikes often break off. They grow back the next day, so it is not bothered by the temporary loss.
In an attempt to hide itself, it will run around at top speed to kick up a blinding dust storm.
It curls up, then rolls into foes with its back. Its sharp spines inflict severe damage.

29.text: Although small, its venomous barbs render this Pokémon dangerous. The female has smaller horns.
Females are more sensitive to smells than males. While foraging, they’ll use their whiskers to check wind direction and stay downwind of predators.
Although not very combative, it will torment its foes with poison spikes if it is threatened in any way.
While it does not prefer to fight, even one drop of the poison it secretes from barbs can be fatal.

30.text: The female's horn develops slowly. Prefers physical attacks such as clawing and biting.
When resting deep in its burrow, its thorns always retract. This is proof that it is relaxed.
If the group is threatened, these Pokémon will band together to assault enemies with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.
When it senses danger, it raises all the barbs on its body. These barbs grow slower than Nidorino’s.

31.text: Its hard scales provide strong protection. It uses its hefty bulk to execute powerful moves.
It is adept at sending foes flying with harsh tackles using its tough, scaly body. This Pokémon is at its strongest when it is defending its young.
It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.
The body is covered by stiff, needlelike scales. If it becomes excited, the needles bristle outwards.

32.text: Stiffens its ears to sense danger. The larger its horns, the more powerful its secreted venom.
Small but brave, this Pokémon will hold its ground and even risk its life in battle to protect the female it’s friendly with.
Its large ears are flapped like wings when it is listening to distant sounds. It extends toxic barbs when angered.
Its large ears are always kept upright. If it senses danger, it will attack with a poisonous sting.

33.text: An aggressive Pokémon that is quick to attack. The horn on its head secretes a powerful venom.
It raises its big ears to check its surroundings. If it senses anything, it attacks immediately.
It is easily angered. By swinging its well- developed horn wildly, it can even punch through diamond.
It has a violent disposition and stabs foes with its horn, which oozes poison upon impact.

34.text: It uses its powerful tail in battle to smash, constrict, then break the prey’s bones.
It is recognized by its rock-hard hide and its extended horn. Be careful with the horn, as it contains venom.
Its steel-like hide adds to its powerful tackle. Its horns are so hard, they can pierce a diamond.
One swing of its mighty tail can snap a telephone pole as if it were a matchstick.

35.text: Its magical and cute appeal has many admirers. It is rare and found only in certain areas.
Though rarely seen, it becomes easier to spot, for some reason, on the night of a full moon.
They’re popular, but they’re rare. Trainers who show them off recklessly may be targeted by thieves.
Adored for their cute looks and playfulness. They are thought to be rare, as they do not appear often.

36.text: A timid fairy Pokémon that is rarely seen, it will run and hide the moment it senses people.
Their ears are sensitive enough to hear a pin drop from over a mile away, so they’re usually found in quiet places.
Legend says that on clear, quiet nights, it listens for the voices of its kin living on the moon. I, too, often think of my homeland, so far away.
They don’t like to reveal themselves in front of people. They live quietly in packs deep in the mountains.

37.text: At the time of birth, it has just one tail. The tail splits from its tip as it grows older.
If it is attacked by an enemy that is stronger than itself, it feigns injury to fool the enemy and escapes.
Its beautiful tails have made it very popular. However, if it’s not brushed diligently, it will be a mass of tangles before you know it.
While young, it has six gorgeous tails. When it grows, several new tails are sprouted.

38.text: Very smart and very vengeful. Grabbing one of its many tails could result in a 1,000-year curse.
The flickering flames it spews from its mouth leave its opponents hypnotized. Then, this extremely intelligent Pokémon attacks.
It is vindictive and relentless by nature. Those who cross it even once will be cursed for a thousand years, along with their descendants.
According to an enduring legend, nine noble saints were united and reincarnated as this Pokémon.

39.text: When its huge eyes light up, it sings a mysteriously soothing melody that lulls its enemies to sleep.
The songs they sing are totally different depending on the region they live in. Some even sound like they’re shouting!
Looking into its cute, round eyes makes it start singing a song so pleasant listeners can’t help but fall asleep.
If it inflates to sing a lullaby, it can perform longer and cause sure drowsiness in its audience.

40.text: The body is soft and rubbery. When angered, it will suck in air and inflate itself to an enormous size.
Their fur feels so good that if two of them snuggle together, they won’t want to be separated.
When it gets angry, it inhales with all its might, and its body gradually inflates. Sometimes they can grow 20 times larger!
Its fur is extremely fine, dense, and supple. The exquisitely pleasant fur conveys an image of luxury.

41.text: Forms colonies in perpetually dark places. Uses ultrasonic waves to identify and approach targets.
Their skin is so thin that they’ll be burned if sunlight hits them. When it gets cold out, they gather together to warm one another’s bodies.
During the day, it gathers with others and hangs from the ceilings of old buildings and caves.
Even though it has no eyes, it can sense obstacles using ultrasonic waves it emits from its mouth.

42.text: Once it strikes, it will not stop draining energy from the victim even if it gets too heavy to fly.
Its thick fangs are hollow like straws, making them unexpectedly fragile. These fangs are specialized for sucking blood.
They can suck down over 10 ounces of blood in one go. They have been known to drink so much blood that they can no longer fly.
It loves the blood of humans and Pokémon. It flies around at night in search of neck veins.

43.text: During the day, it keeps its face buried in the ground. At night, it wanders around sowing its seeds.
It may be mistaken for a clump of weeds. If you try to yank it out of the ground, it shrieks horribly.
Its scientific name is “Oddium Wanderus.” At night, it is said to walk nearly 1,000 feet on its two roots.
This Pokémon grows by absorbing moonlight. During the daytime, it buries itself in the ground, leaving only its leaves exposed to avoid detection by its enemies.

44.text: The fluid that oozes from its mouth isn’t drool. It is a nectar that is used to attract prey.
Smells incredibly foul! However, around 1 out of 1,000 people enjoy sniffing its nose- bending stink.
What appears to be drool is actually sweet honey. It is very sticky and clings stubbornly if touched.
Its pistils exude an incredibly foul odor. The horrid stench can cause fainting at a distance of 1.25 miles.

45.text: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.
The bud bursts into bloom with a bang. It then starts scattering allergenic, poisonous pollen.
Its petals are the largest in the world. It fiendishly scatters allergy-causing pollen from its petals.
Flaps its broad flower petals to scatter its poisonous pollen. The flapping sound is very loud.

46.text: Burrows to suck tree roots. The mushrooms on its back grow by drawing nutrients from the bug host.
As its body grows large, oriental mushrooms named tochukaso start sprouting out of its back.
The mushrooms, known as tochukaso, are controlling the bug. Even if the bug bugs the mushrooms, they tell it to bug off.
Mushrooms called tochukaso sprout from its back. They can be dried and powdered to make a medicine used to extend life.

47.text: A host-parasite pair in which the parasite mushroom has taken over the host bug. Prefers damp places.
It scatters toxic spores from its mushroom cap. Once harvested, these spores can be steeped and boiled down to prepare herbal medicines.
Its poisonous spores are also used in traditional medicine. Apparently, spores produced in Alola are not of very good quality.
The bug is mostly dead, with the mushroom on its back having become the main body. If the mushroom comes off, the bug stops moving.

48.text: Lives in the shadows of tall trees where it eats insects. It is attracted by light at night.
Its coat of thin, stiff hair that covers its entire body is said to have evolved for protection. Its large eyes never fail to spot even miniscule prey.
Its eyes act as radar, enabling it to be active in darkness. The eyes can also shoot powerful beams.
Its large eyes act as radars. In a bright place, you can see that they are clusters of many tiny eyes.

49.text: The dustlike scales covering its wings are color-coded to indicate the kinds of poison it has.
The scales it scatters will paralyze anyone who touches them, making that person unable to stand.
The powder on its wings is poisonous if it is dark in hue. If it is light in hue, it causes paralysis.
When it attacks, it flaps its large wings violently to scatter its poisonous powder all around.

50.text: Lives about one yard underground where it feeds on plant roots. It sometimes appears aboveground.
It burrows through the ground at a shallow depth. It leaves raised earth in its wake, making it easy to spot.
It travels through tunnels that it digs underground. It hates sunlight, so it comes out only after the sun goes down.
It prefers dark places. It spends most of its time underground, though it may pop up in caves.

51.text: A team of Diglett triplets. It triggers huge earthquakes by burrowing 60 miles underground.
Because the triplets originally split from one body, they think exactly alike. They work cooperatively to burrow endlessly through the ground.
While the three of them normally get along splendidly, on rare occasions a huge fight will break out over which head gets to eat first.
Its three heads bob separately up and down to loosen the soil nearby, making it easier for it to burrow.

52.text: Adores circular objects. Wanders the streets on a nightly basis to look for dropped loose change.
It is nocturnal in nature. If it spots something shiny, its eyes glitter brightly.
It loves anything that shines. It especially adores coins that it picks up and secretly hoards.
When visiting a junkyard, you may catch sight of it having an intense fight with Murkrow over shiny objects.

53.text: Although its fur has many admirers, it is tough to raise as a pet because of its fickle meanness.
This Pokémon is popular with rich people. It’s also targeted by hunters who are after the jewel in its forehead.
Behind its lithe, elegant appearance lies a barbaric side. It will tear apart its prey on a mere whim.
Many adore it for its sophisticated air. However, it will lash out and scratch for little reason.

54.text: While lulling its enemies with its vacant look, this wily Pokémon will use psychokinetic powers.
As a result of headaches so fierce they cause it to cry, it sometimes uses psychokinesis without meaning to.
It has mystical powers but doesn’t recall that it has used them. That is why it always looks puzzled.
The only time it can use its psychic power is when its sleeping brain cells happen to wake.

55.text: Often seen swimming elegantly by lakeshores. It is often mistaken for the Japanese monster Kappa.
When it swims at full speed using its long, webbed limbs, its forehead somehow begins to glow.
A Pokémon that lives in lakes. It swims faster than any human swimming champion.
Its slim and long limbs end in broad flippers. They are used for swimming gracefully in lakes.

56.text: Extremely quick to anger. It could be docile one moment, then thrashing away the next instant.
Light and agile on its feet, and ferocious in temperament. When angered, it flies into an uncontrollable frenzy.
It’s unsafe to approach if it gets violently enraged for no reason and can’t distinguish friends from foes.
It lives in groups in the treetops. If it loses sight of its group, it becomes infuriated by its loneliness.

57.text: Always furious and tenacious to boot. It will not abandon chasing its quarry until it is caught.
The blood vessels in its brain are sturdier than those of other Pokémon, so it can stay healthy despite its constant raging.
If approached while asleep, it may awaken and angrily give chase in a groggy state of semi-sleep.
It will never forgive opponents who have angered it. Even after it has beaten them down until they can’t move, it never ever forgives.

58.text: Very protective of its territory. It will bark and bite to repel intruders from its space.
They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.
A Pokémon with a loyal nature. It will remain motionless until it is given an order by its Trainer.
It controls a big territory. If it detects an unknown smell, it roars loudly to force out the intruder.

59.text: A Pokémon that has been admired since the past for its beauty. It runs agilely as if on wings.
Legends tell of its fighting alongside a general and conquering a whole country.
There are so many old tales about them that they’re called legendary Pokémon, but there are way more of them around than you’d expect.
Overflowing with beauty and majesty, this strong Pokémon appears in ancient Eastern folklore.

60.text: Its newly grown legs prevent it from running. It appears to prefer swimming than trying to stand.
Its slick black skin is thin and damp. A part of its internal organs can be seen through the skin as a spiral pattern.
In rivers with fast-flowing water, this Pokémon will cling to a rock by using its thick lips, which act like a suction cup.
Despite the danger, it wants to come up on land. So it does its best to waddle along, but when an enemy finds it, it rushes back to the water.

61.text: Capable of living in or out of water. When out of water, it sweats to keep its body slimy.
The swirl on its belly subtly undulates. Staring at it may gradually cause drowsiness.
Though it is skilled at walking, it prefers to live underwater where there is less danger.
It marches over the land in search of bug Pokémon to eat. Then it takes them underwater so it can dine on them where it’s safe.

62.text: An adept swimmer at both the front crawl and breast stroke. Easily overtakes the best human swimmers.
Its percentage of body fat is nearly zero. Its body is entirely muscle, which makes it heavy and forces its swimming prowess to develop.
It’s quite a gifted swimmer, even among Water-type Pokémon, but it normally spends its time on land.
With its extremely tough muscles, it can keep swimming in the Pacific Ocean without resting.

63.text: Using its ability to read minds, it will identify impending danger and TELEPORT to safety.
It uses various psychic powers even while it’s sleeping, so you can’t tell whether or not it’s awake.
Even while asleep, it maintains a telepathic radar. It teleports when it is threatened.
If it decides to TELEPORT randomly, it creates the illusion that it has created copies of itself.

64.text: It emits special alpha waves from its body that induce headaches just by being close by.
If one is nearby, an eerie shadow appears on TV screens. Seeing the shadow is said to bring bad luck.
A theory exists that this Pokémon was a young boy who couldn’t control his psychic powers and ended up transformed into this Pokémon.
It stares at a silver spoon to amplify its psychic powers before it lets loose. Apparently, gold spoons are no good.

65.text: Its brain can outperform a supercomputer. Its intelligence quotient is said to be 5,000.
It has an IQ of 5000. It calculates many things in order to gain the edge in every battle.
If it trusts someone deeply, it will let them have one of its spoons. Anything you eat with that spoon is apparently delicious.
It does not like physical attacks very much. Instead, it freely uses extrasensory powers to defeat foes.

66.text: Loves to build its muscles. It trains in all styles of martial arts to become even stronger.
Once this Pokémon has gained enough confidence and muscle from training with its friends, it challenges Makuhita to a battle.
Always brimming with power, it passes time by lifting boulders. Doing so makes it even stronger.
It likes food that’s highly nutritious because its instincts drive it to build muscle efficiently.

67.text: Its muscular body is so powerful, it must wear a power-save belt to be able to regulate its motions.
A sturdy creature boasting a robust physique and boundless stamina. Loves training above all else and voluntarily assists with tasks such as construction and clearing land.
This tough Pokémon always stays in the zone. Its muscles become thicker after every battle.
It happily carries heavy cargo to toughen up. It willingly does hard work for people.

68.text: Using its heavy muscles, it throws powerful punches that can send the victim clear over the horizon.
In close combat, its four arms afford it offensive and defensive supremacy. In but a blink, this valiant Pokémon can overwhelm its foes with more than 1,000 blows from its fists.
It is impossible to defend against punches and chops doled out by its four arms. Its fighting spirit flares up when it faces a tough opponent.
It can knock a train flying with a punch. However, it is terrible at delicate work using its fingers.

69.text: A carnivorous Pokémon that traps and eats bugs. It uses its root feet to soak up needed moisture.
Even though its body is extremely skinny, it is blindingly fast when catching its prey.
Prefers hot and humid places. It ensnares tiny insects with its vines and devours them.
If it notices anything that moves, it immediately flings its vine at the object.

70.text: It spits out Poison Powder to immobilize the enemy and then finishes it with a spray of Acid.
When it's hungry, it swings its razor-sharp leaves, slicing up any unlucky object nearby for food.
When hungry, it swallows anything that moves. Its hapless prey is melted inside by strong acids.
Even though it is filled with ACID, it does not melt because it also oozes a neutralizing fluid.

71.text: Said to live in huge colonies deep in jungles, although no one has ever returned from there.
Once ingested into this Pokémon’s body, even the hardest object will melt into nothing.
It pools in its mouth a fluid with a honey-like scent, which is really an acid that dissolves anything.
Acid that has dissolved many prey becomes sweeter, making it even more effective at attracting prey.

72.text: Drifts in shallow seas. Anglers who hook them by accident are often punished by its stinging acid.
It can sometimes be found all dry and shriveled up on a beach. Toss it back into the sea to revive it.
Its body is virtually composed of water. It shoots strange beams from its crystal-like eyes.
It drifts aimlessly in waves. Very difficult to see in water, it may not be noticed until it stings.

73.text: The tentacles are normally kept short. On hunts, they are extended to ensnare and immobilize prey.
Although these Pokémon are rare, when a large outbreak of them occurs, all fish Pokémon disappear from the surrounding sea.
When its 80 feelers absorb water, it stretches to become like a net to entangle its prey.
It has 80 tentacles that move about freely. They can sting, causing poisoning and sharp, stabbing pain.

74.text: Found in fields and mountains. Mistaking them for boulders, people often step or trip on them.
It uses its arms to steadily climb steep mountain paths. It swings its fists around if angered.
Proud of their sturdy bodies, they bash against each other in a contest to prove whose is harder.
Many live on mountain trails and remain half buried while keeping an eye on climbers.

75.text: Rolls down slopes to move. It rolls over any obstacle without slowing or changing its direction.
This slow-footed Pokémon moves by curling up and rolling instead of walking. With enough momentum, its speed can exceed 60 mph.
Mossy rocks are its favorite food. It can devour a ton a day while crunching loudly.
Dwells in holes dug into sheer walls of stone. It enjoys rolling down slopes as though it were a boulder during a rockfall, so keep an eye upward while traversing mountain roads.

76.text: Its boulder-like body is extremely hard. It can easily withstand dynamite blasts without damage.
Once a year, this Pokémon molts, and its shed shell returns to the soil. This process creates enriched soil, so farmers collect the shells.
It tumbles down mountains, leaving grooves from peak to base. Stay clear of these grooves.
Once it sheds its skin, its body turns tender and whitish. Its hide hardens when it’s exposed to air.

77.text: Its hooves are 10 times harder than diamonds. It can trample anything completely flat in little time.
These Pokémon live in herds out in the grassland. Newborn foals lack their fiery manes, which will develop about an hour after birth.
Training by jumping over grass that grows longer every day has made it a world-class jumper.
Capable of jumping incredibly high. Its hooves and sturdy legs absorb the impact of a hard landing.

78.text: Very competitive, this Pokémon will chase anything that moves fast in the hopes of racing it.
When at an all-out gallop, its blazing mane sparkles, enhancing its beautiful appearance.
It has astounding acceleration. From a standstill, it can reach top speed within 10 steps.
The fastest runner becomes the leader, and it decides the herd’s pace and direction of travel.

79.text: Incredibly slow and dopey. It takes 5 seconds for it to feel pain when under attack.
It is always vacantly lost in thought, but no one knows what it is thinking about. It is good at fishing with its tail.
Although their tails, which fall off naturally, can easily be found lying around, they’re a precious ingredient for cooking.
A sweet sap leaks from its tail’s tip. Although not nutritious, the tail is pleasant to chew on.

80.text: The SHELLDER that is latched onto SLOWPOKE's tail is said to feed on the host's left over scraps.
It spaces out while gazing at the sea. With Shellder’s poison flowing through its body, it becomes even spacier.
Its tail has a SHELLDER firmly attached with a bite. As a result, the tail can’t be used for fishing anymore. This forces it to reluctantly swim and catch prey.
Spacing out is basically all it does. It turns back into Slowpoke if its tail, along with Shellder, breaks off.

81.text: Uses antigravity to stay suspended. Appears without warning and uses THUNDER WAVE and similar moves.
It is attracted by electromagnetic waves. It may approach Trainers if they are using their Pokégear.
The faster the units at its sides rotate, the greater the magnetic force they generate.
A bizarre Pokémon with but a single eye embedded in an iron sphere. I suspect this creature levitates due to the magnetism it emits from its arms, which resemble horseshoe-shaped magnets.

82.text: Formed by several MAGNEMITEs linked together. They frequently appear when sunspots flare up.
Three Magnemite gathered to evolve into this Pokémon. The source of much vexation on my part, as its powerful magnetism destroys my research equipment.
Generates strange radio signals. It raises the temperature by 3.6F degrees within 3,300 feet.
Three MAGNEMITE are linked by a strong magnetic force. Earaches will occur if you get too close.

83.text: The sprig of green onions it holds is its weapon. It is used much like a metal sword.
In order to prevent their extinction, more people have made an effort to breed these Pokémon.
Lives where reedy plants grow. They are rarely seen, so it's thought their numbers are decreasing.
It is always seen with a stick from a plant. Apparently, there are good sticks and bad sticks. This Pokémon occasionally fights with others over choice sticks.

84.text: A bird that makes up for its poor flying with its fast foot speed. Leaves giant footprints.
Even while eating or sleeping, one of the heads remains always vigilant for any sign of danger. When threatened, it flees at over 60 miles per hour.
It lives on a grassy plain where it can see a long way. If it sees an enemy, it runs away at 60 mph.
By alternately raising and lowering its two heads, it balances itself to be more stable while running.

85.text: Uses its three brains to execute complex plans. While two heads sleep, one head stays awake.
A peculiar Pokémon species with three heads. It vigorously races across grassy plains even in arid seasons with little rainfall.
It collects data and plans three times as wisely, but it may think too much and become immobilized.
An odd species that is rarely found. The three heads respectively represent joy, sadness, and anger.

86.text: The protruding horn on its head is very hard. It is used for bashing through thick ice.
Loves freezing cold conditions. Relishes swimming in a frigid climate of around 14F degrees.
The light blue fur that covers it keeps it protected against the cold. It loves iceberg- filled oceans.
Thanks to its thick fat, cold seas don’t bother it at all, but it gets tired pretty easily in warm waters.

87.text: Stores thermal energy in its body. Swims at a steady 8 knots even in intensely cold waters.
It loves frigid seas with ice floes. It uses its long tail to change swimming direction quickly.
It sleeps under shallow ocean waters during the day, then looks for food at night when it's cold.
Its body is covered with a pure white fur. The colder the weather, the more active it becomes.

88.text: Appears in filthy areas. Thrives by sucking up polluted sludge that is pumped out of factories.
When two of these Pokémon's bodies are combined together, new poisons are created.
It was born from sludge on the ocean floor. In a sterile environment, the germs within its body can’t multiply, and it dies.
Its main source of food is the slimy industrial waste of factories. This Pokémon’s numbers have been decreasing in recent years.

89.text: Thickly covered with a filthy, vile sludge. It is so toxic, even its footprints contain poison.
Because they scatter germs everywhere, they’ve long been targeted for extermination, leading to a steep decline in their population.
After recent environmental improvements, this Pokémon is now hardly seen at all. People speculate that it may go extinct at some point.
Their food sources have decreased, and their numbers have declined sharply. Sludge ponds are being built to prevent their extinction.

90.text: Its hard shell repels any kind of attack. It is vulnerable only when its shell is open.
Grains of sand trapped in its shells mix with its body fluids to form beautiful pearls.
The sand that accumulates inside its shell eventually becomes a pearl. But the pearl gets in the way, so it spits it out and discards it.
It swims backward by opening and closing its two shells. Its large tongue is always kept hanging out.

91.text: When attacked, it launches its horns in quick volleys. Its innards have never been seen.
Excavation of the tombs of ancient hunting tribes has turned up many spears tipped with spikes that had fallen off this Pokémon’s shell.
Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.
For protection, it uses its harder- than-diamonds shell. It also shoots spikes from the shell.

92.text: Almost invisible, this gaseous Pokémon cloaks the target and puts it to sleep without notice.
With its gas-like body, it can sneak into any place it desires. However, it can be blown away by wind.
Said to appear in decrepit, deserted buildings. It has no real shape, as it appears to be made of a gas.
Gaseous and completely impalpable. Also highly dangerous— inhaling part of its poisonous body will cause one to faint instantly.

93.text: Because of its ability to slip through block walls, it is said to be from another dimension.
By licking, it saps the victim’s life. It causes shaking that won’t stop until the victim’s demise.
It strikes at humans from total darkness. Those licked by its cold tongue grow weaker with each passing day until they die.
It fears the light and revels in the dark. It may be on the verge of extinction in cities that stay brightly lit at night.

94.text: Under a full moon, this Pokémon likes to mimic the shadows of people and laugh at their fright.
It is said to emerge from darkness to steal the lives of those who become lost in mountains.
It apparently wishes for a traveling companion. Since it was once human itself, it tries to create one by taking the lives of other humans.
To steal the life of its target, it slips into the prey’s shadow and silently waits for an opportunity.

95.text: As it grows, the stone portions of its body harden to become similar to a diamond, but colored black.
When it travels underground, it causes rumbling and tremors. It can move at 50 mph.
Opening its large mouth, it ingests massive amounts of soil and creates long tunnels.
It usually lives underground. It searches for food while boring its way through the ground at 50 miles per hour.

96.text: Puts enemies to sleep then eats their dreams. Occasionally gets sick from eating bad dreams.
When it twitches its nose, it can tell where someone is sleeping and what that person is dreaming about.
It finds really fun dreams tasty. When it makes friends with people, it may show them the most delicious dreams it’s ever eaten.
It can be spotted near recreational facilities, intending to eat the pleasant dreams of children who enjoyed themselves there that day.

97.text: Avoid eye contact if you come across one. It will try to put you to sleep by using its pendulum.
As a matter of course, it makes anyone it meets fall asleep and has a taste of their dreams. Anyone having a good dream, it carries off.
Always holding a pendulum that it rocks at a steady rhythm, it causes drowsiness in anyone nearby.
Seeing its swinging pendulum can induce sleep in three seconds, even in someone who just woke up.

98.text: Its pincers are not only powerful weapons, they are used for balance when walking sideways.
If it is unable to find food, it will absorb nutrients by swallowing a mouthful of sand.
It can be found near the sea. The large pincers grow back if they are torn out of their sockets.
If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.

99.text: The large pincer has 10000 hp of crushing power. However, its huge size makes it unwieldy to use.
Its oversized claw is very powerful, but when it’s not in battle, the claw just gets in the way.
One claw grew massively and is as hard as steel. It has 10,000-horsepower strength. However, it is too heavy.
Its pincers grow peculiarly large. If it lifts the pincers too fast, it loses its balance and staggers.

100.text: Usually found in power plants. Easily mistaken for a POKé BALL, they have zapped many people.
It rolls to move. If the ground is uneven, a sudden jolt from hitting a bump can cause it to explode.
It was discovered when Poké Balls were introduced. It is said that there is some connection.
An enigmatic Pokémon that happens to bear a resemblance to a Poké Ball. When excited, it discharges the electric current it has stored in its belly, then lets out a great, uproarious laugh.

101.text: It stores electric energy under very high pressure. It often explodes with little or no provocation.
The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.
It is dangerous. If it has too much electricity and has nothing to do, it amuses itself by exploding.
They appear in great numbers at electric power plants. Because they feed on electricity, they cause massive and chaotic blackouts in nearby cities.

102.text: Often mistaken for eggs. When disturbed, they quickly gather and attack in swarms.
The shell is very durable. Even if it cracks, it can survive without spilling the contents.
Six of them together form a full-fledged Pokémon. It’s often hunted by Crabrawler, but uses psychokinesis to drive it off.
The heads attract each other and spin around. There must be 6 heads for it to maintain balance.

103.text: Legend has it that on rare occasions, one of its heads will drop off and continue on as an EXEGGCUTE.
Its three heads think independently. However, they are friendly and never appear to squabble.
Its cries are very noisy. This is because each of the 3 heads thinks about whatever it likes.
Each of its heads has its own will. They use telepathy to discuss their plans before coming to a joint decision.

104.text: Because it never removes its skull helmet, no one has ever seen this Pokémon’s real face.
When it thinks of its deceased mother, it weeps loudly. Mandibuzz that hear its cries will attack it from the air.
If it is sad or lonely, the skull it wears shakes and emits a plaintive and mournful sound.
It wears its mother’s skull on its head, so no one knows what its bare face looks like. However, it’s clear that it’s always crying.

105.text: The bone it holds is its key weapon. It throws the bone skillfully like a boomerang to KO targets.
They thump their bones rhythmically to communicate among themselves. There are nearly 50 different rhythmic patterns.
Originally, it was weak and timid. After evolution, its temperament becomes violent, and it begins to wield bones as weapons.
It has been seen pounding boulders with the bone it carries in order to tap out messages to others.

106.text: When in a hurry, its legs lengthen progressively. It runs smoothly with extra-long, loping strides.
This amazing Pokémon has an awesome sense of balance. It can kick in succession from any position.
Its legs can stretch double. First-time foes are startled by its extensible reach.
When kicking, the sole of its foot turns as hard as a diamond on impact and destroys its enemy.

107.text: While apparently doing nothing, it fires punches in lightning-fast volleys that are impossible to see.
Its punches slice the air. They are launched at such high speed, even a slight graze could cause a burn.
To increase the strength of all its punch moves, it spins its arms just before making contact.
The arm-twisting punches it throws pulverize even concrete. It rests after three minutes of fighting.

108.text: Its tongue can be extended like a chameleon’s. It leaves a tingling sensation when it licks enemies.
If this Pokémon’s sticky saliva gets on you and you don’t clean it off, an intense itch will set in. The itch won’t go away, either.
Whenever it sees something unfamiliar, it always licks the object because it memorizes things by texture and taste. It is somewhat put off by sour things.
Instead of hands, it uses its tongue, which is twice its height. Its sticky saliva grips anything.

109.text: Because it stores several kinds of toxic gases in its body, it is prone to exploding without warning.
If one gets close enough to it when it expels poisonous gas, the gas swirling inside it can be seen.
The poisonous gases it contains are a little bit lighter than air, keeping it slightly airborne.
Its thin, filmy body is filled with gases that cause constant sniffles, coughs and teary eyes.

110.text: It lives and grows by absorbing dust, germs and poison gases that are contained in toxic waste and garbage.
If one of the twin Koffing inflates, the other one deflates. It constantly mixes its poisonous gases.
Inhaling toxic fumes from trash and mixing them inside its body lets it spread an even fouler stench.
Top-grade perfume is made using its internal poison gases by diluting them to the highest level.

111.text: Its massive bones are 1000 times harder than human bones. It can easily knock a trailer flying.
A Pokémon with a one-track mind. Once it charges, it won’t stop running until it falls asleep.
Ludicrously strong—when it butts heads with a mountain, it is the mountain that shatters. But its short legs struggle with turns, and it is incapable of stopping unless it collides with something.
It doesn’t care if there is anything in its way. It just charges and destroys all obstacles.

112.text: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 3,600 degrees.
Its brain developed after it stood up on its hind legs. Its drill horn bores tunnels through solid rock.
By lightly spinning its drill- like horn, it can easily shatter even a diamond in the rough.
Rapidly rotates its horn to bore through bedrock. It swaggers around volcanic regions, protected from the lava's heat by its tough, armorlike hide.

113.text: A rare and elusive Pokémon that is said to bring happiness to those who manage to get it.
People try to catch it for its extremely nutritious eggs, but it rarely can be found.
Not only are these Pokémon fast runners, they’re also few in number, so anyone who finds one must be lucky indeed.
This purehearted Pokémon shares its eggs with the injured.

114.text: The whole body is swathed with wide vines that are similar to seaweed. Its vines shake as it walks.
Hidden beneath a tangle of vines that grows nonstop even if the vines are torn off, this Pokémon’s true appearance remains a mystery.
It is shrouded by blue vines. No one has seen the face hidden behind this growth of vines.
Its vines snap off easily and painlessly if they are grabbed, allowing it to make a quick getaway. The lost vines are replaced by new growth the very next day.

115.text: The infant rarely ventures out of its mother's protective pouch until it is 3 years old.
Raises its young in its belly pouch. Won’t run from any fight to keep its young protected.
To protect its young, it will never give up during battle, no matter how badly wounded it is.
To avoid crushing the baby it carries in its pouch, it always sleeps standing up.

116.text: Known to shoot down flying bugs with precision blasts of ink from the surface of the water.
When they're in a safe location, they can be seen playfully tangling their tails together.
If attacked by a larger enemy, it quickly swims to safety by adeptly controlling its well-developed dorsal fin.
It maintains balance using its tail, which is wound up like a coil. It may spray ink from its mouth.

117.text: Capable of swimming backwards by rapidly flapping its wing-like pectoral fins and stout tail.
The poisonous barbs all over its body are highly valued as ingredients for making traditional herbal medicine. It shows no mercy to anything approaching its nest.
An examination of its cells revealed the presence of a gene not found in HORSEA. It became a hot topic.
The male raises the young. If it is approached, it uses its toxic spikes to fend off the intruder.

118.text: Its tail fin billows like an elegant ballroom dress, giving it the nickname of “The Water Queen.”
When the weather grows warm, they form groups and swim upriver. This sight serves as a poetic reminder that spring has arrived.
A strong swimmer, it is capable of swimming nonstop up fast streams at a steady speed of five knots per hour.
During spawning season, they swim gracefully in the water, searching for their perfect mate.

119.text: In the autumn spawning season, they can be seen swimming powerfully up rivers and creeks.
Its horn spins like a drill to steadily hollow out rocks—even harder ones. The coloration of the male is more vivid.
When the weather grows cold, its whole body flushes a deep red. This sight serves as a poetic reminder that autumn has arrived.
Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.

120.text: An enigmatic Pokémon that can effortlessly regenerate any appendage it loses in battle.
At night, the center of its body slowly flickers with the same rhythm as a human heartbeat.
This Pokémon gets nibbled on by Lumineon and others. Thanks to its red core, it regenerates fast, so it’s unconcerned by their snack attacks.
As long as the center section is unharmed, it can grow back fully even if it is chopped to bits.

121.text: Its central core glows with the seven colors of the rainbow. Some people value the core as a gem.
Its shining core is thought to receive and transmit enigmatic signals. It has been known to cause headaches in those who approach it.
Its unusual body shape, reminiscent of abstract art, led local people to spread rumors that this Pokémon may be an invader from outer space.
It rotates its geometrically shaped body to swim through the water. It always seems to be sending out mysterious radio waves.

122.text: If interrupted while it is miming, it will slap around the offender with its broad hands.
Its fingertips emit a peculiar force field that hardens air to create an actual wall.
Always practices its pantomime act. It makes enemies believe something exists that really doesn't.
It’s known for its top-notch pantomime skills. It protects itself from all sorts of attacks by emitting auras from its fingers to create walls.

123.text: With ninja-like agility and speed, it can create the illusion that there is more than one.
The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.
When it moves, it leaves only a blur. If it hides in grass, its protective colors make it invisible.
While young, they live together deep in the mountains, training themselves in how to fight with their scythes and move at high speeds.

124.text: It seductively wiggles its hips as it walks. It can cause people to dance in unison with it.
It speaks using a language that sounds human. Research is under way to determine what is being said.
It rocks its body rhythmically. It appears to alter the rhythm depending on how it is feeling.
It has several different cry patterns, each of which seems to have its own meaning.

125.text: Normally found near power plants, they can wander away and cause major blackouts in cities.
Its body constantly discharges electricity. Getting close to it will make your hair stand on end.
With the coming of a storm, many of these Pokémon will gather under tall trees and sit there waiting for lightning to strike.
Electricity leaks from it in amounts far greater than the amount of electricity it eats.

126.text: Its body always burns with an orange glow that enables it to hide perfectly among flames.
Found near the mouth of a volcano. This fire-breather’s body temperature is nearly 2,200 degrees Fahrenheit.
It moves more frequently in hot areas. It can heal itself by dipping its wound into lava.
It dislikes cold places, so it blows scorching flames to make the environment suitable for itself.

127.text: If it fails to crush the victim in its pincers, it will swing it around and toss it hard.
Its two long pincer horns are powerful. Once they grip an enemy, they won’t release until the foe is torn.
These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.
When the temperature drops at night, it sleeps on treetops or among roots where it is well hidden.

128.text: When it targets an enemy, it charges furiously while whipping its body with its long tails.
They fight each other by locking horns. The herd’s protector takes pride in its battle-scarred horns.
A rowdy Pokémon with a lot of stamina. Once running, it won’t stop until it hits something.
Once it takes aim at its foe, it makes a headlong charge. It is famous for its violent nature.

129.text: In the distant past, it was somewhat stronger than the horribly weak descendants that exist today.
For no reason, it jumps and splashes about, making it easy for predators like PIDGEOTTO to catch it mid-jump.
This weak and pathetic Pokémon gets easily pushed along rivers when there are strong currents.
Thanks to their strong hold on life, dirty water doesn’t bother them at all. They live in waters all over the world!

130.text: Rarely seen in the wild. Huge and vicious, it is capable of destroying entire cities in a rage.
It has an extremely aggressive nature. The Hyper Beam it shoots from its mouth totally incinerates all targets.
Once it appears, it goes on a rampage. It remains enraged until it demolishes everything around it.
It appears whenever there is world conflict, burning down any place it travels through.

131.text: A Pokémon that has been overhunted almost to extinction. It can ferry people across the water.
They have gentle hearts. Because they rarely fight, many have been caught. Their number has dwindled.
Its high intelligence enables it to comprehend human speech. When it’s in a good mood, it sings in its beautiful voice.
It likes swimming around with people on its back. In the Alola region, it’s an important means of transportation over water.

132.text: Capable of copying an enemy's genetic code to instantly transform itself into a duplicate of the enemy.
Its transformation ability is perfect. However, if made to laugh, it can’t maintain its disguise.
It can reconstitute its entire cellular structure to change into what it sees, but it returns to normal when it relaxes.
When it spots an enemy, its body transfigures into an almost-perfect copy of its opponent.

133.text: Its genetic code is irregular. It may mutate if it is exposed to radiation from element STONEs.
An extremely rare Pokémon that may evolve in a number of different ways depending on stimuli.
Its genes are easily influenced by its surroundings. Even its face starts to look like that of its Trainer.
Possessing an unbalanced and unstable genetic makeup, it conceals many possible evolutions.

134.text: Lives close to water. Its long tail is ridged with a fin which is often mistaken for a mermaid’s.
It has evolved to be suitable for an aquatic life. It can invisibly melt away into water.
Blending in with the water and erasing all signs of its presence, it patiently waits for its prey, fish Pokémon.
It detects nearby moisture with its fin. When its fin begins trembling rapidly, that means rain will fall in a few hours.

135.text: It accumulates negative ions in the atmosphere to blast out 10,000-volt lightning bolts.
A sensitive Pokémon that easily becomes sad or angry. Every time its mood changes, it charges power.
Bristles its fur into sharp, needlelike points when enraged. One can hear electricity crackle in its breath when it exhales.
Its cells generate weak power that is amplified by its fur’s static electricity to drop thunderbolts. The bristling fur is made of electrically charged needles.

136.text: When storing thermal energy in its body, its temperature could soar to over 1600 degrees.
When it catches prey or finds berries, it breathes fire on them until they’re well done, and then it gobbles them up.
If it inhales deeply, that’s a sign it’s about to attack. Prepare to be hit by flames of over 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit!
Inhaled air is carried to its flame sac, heated, and exhaled as fire that reaches over 3,000 degrees F.

137.text: A Pokémon that consists entirely of programming code. Capable of moving freely in cyberspace.
It has no discernible heartbeat and does not seem to draw breath, and yet it appears to function without issue. I cannot even begin to explain this utterly bizarre anomaly.
Roughly 20 years ago, it was artificially created, utilizing the latest technology of the time.
It can convert its body into digital data, which enables it to enter cyberspace.

138.text: Although long extinct, in rare cases, it can be genetically resurrected from fossils.
This Pokémon from ancient times is said to have navigated the sea by adeptly twisting its 10 tentacles.
In prehistoric times, it swam on the sea floor, eating plankton. Its fossils are sometimes found.
It was restored from an ancient fossil. Those Helix Fossils are excavated from areas that were once oceans long, long ago.

139.text: A prehistoric Pokémon that died out when its heavy shell made it impossible to catch prey.
Once wrapped around its prey, it never lets go. It eats the prey by tearing at it with sharp fangs.
Its tentacles are highly developed as if they are hands and feet. As soon as it ensnares prey, it bites.
Sharp beaks ring its mouth. Its shell was too big for it to move freely, so it became extinct.

140.text: A Pokémon that was resurrected from a fossil found in what was once the ocean floor eons ago.
It is thought to have inhabited beaches 300 million years ago. It is protected by a stiff shell.
This Pokémon became extinct everywhere, except in a few areas. It protects itself with its hard shell.
On rare occasions, some have been found as fossils which they became while hiding on the ocean floor.

141.text: Its sleek shape is perfect for swimming. It slashes prey with its claws and drains the body fluids.
It was able to swim quickly through the water by compactly folding up its razor-sharp sickles.
Its body had begun to change so it could function on land. But it didn’t adapt in time and went extinct.
It is thought that this Pokémon came onto land because its prey adapted to life on land.

142.text: A ferocious, prehistoric Pokémon that goes for the enemy’s throat with its serrated, sawlike fangs.
It flew through the open skies over the ancient continent as if they were its own. When it touched ground, its walk was weak and slow.
This vicious Pokémon is said to have flown in ancient skies while shrieking high-pitched cries.
Restored from DNA found in amber, this Pokémon exhibited ferocity that was greater than expected. Some casualties resulted.

143.text: Very lazy. Just eats and sleeps. As its rotund bulk builds, it becomes steadily more slothful.
This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.
Will eat anything, even if the food happens to be a little moldy. It never gets an upset stomach.
What sounds like its cry may actually be its snores or the rumblings of its hungry belly.

144.text: A legendary bird Pokémon that is said to appear to doomed people who are lost in icy mountains.
One of the legendary bird Pokémon. With its long tail trailing behind, its flying form is magnificent.
Legendary bird Pokémon. As it flies through the sky, it cools the air, causing snow to fall.
The magnificent, seemingly translucent wings of this legendary bird Pokémon are said to be made of ice.

145.text: A legendary bird Pokémon that is said to appear from clouds while dropping enormous lightning bolts.
This legendary bird Pokémon causes savage thunderstorms by flapping its glittering wings.
One of the legendary bird Pokémon. While it is flying, it makes crackling and snapping sounds.
This legendary bird Pokémon is said to appear when the sky turns dark and lightning showers down.

146.text: Known as the legendary bird of fire. Every flap of its wings creates a dazzling flash of flames.
This legendary bird Pokémon is said to bring early spring to the wintry lands it visits.
There are stories of this Pokémon using its radiant, flame-cloaked wings to light up paths for those lost in the mountains.
This legendary Pokémon scatters embers with every flap of its wings. It is a thrilling sight to behold.

147.text: Long considered a mythical Pokémon until recently, when a small colony was found living underwater.
It is born large to start with. It repeatedly sheds its skin as it steadily grows longer.
It’s still weak, so it lurks on the floor of bodies of water, eating whatever food sinks down and living a quiet life.
After a 10-hour struggle, a fisherman was able to pull one up and confirm its existence.

148.text: A mystical Pokémon that exudes a gentle aura. Has the ability to change climate conditions.
Some say that if you see it at the start of the year, flying through the sky and twisting its body, you’ll be healthy all year long.
It is said to live in seas and lakes. Even though it has no wings, it has been seen flying occasionally.
It is called the divine Pokémon. When its entire body brightens slightly, the weather changes.

149.text: An extremely rarely seen marine Pokémon. Its intelligence is said to match that of humans.
It flies over raging seas as if they were nothing. Observing this, a ship’s captain dubbed this Pokémon “the sea incarnate.”
It can fly in spite of its big and bulky physique. It circles the globe in just 16 hours.
It is said that somewhere in the ocean lies an island where these gather. Only they live there.

150.text: It was created by a scientist after years of horrific gene-splicing and DNA-engineering experiments.
It usually remains motionless to conserve energy, so that it may unleash its full power in battle.
Its DNA is almost the same as Mew’s. However, its size and disposition are vastly different.
Said to rest quietly in an undiscovered cave, this Pokémon was created solely for battling.

151.text: So rare that it is still said to be a mirage by many experts. Only a few people have seen it worldwide.
When viewed through a microscope, this Pokémon’s short, fine, delicate hair can be seen.
Because it can learn any move, some people began research to see if it is the ancestor of all Pokémon.
Apparently, it appears only to those people who are pure of heart and have a strong desire to see it.

152.text: A sweet aroma gently wafts from the leaf on its head. It is docile and loves to soak up the sun’s rays.
Its pleasantly aromatic leaves have the ability to check the humidity and temperature.
It waves its leaf around to keep foes at bay. However, a sweet fragrance also wafts from the leaf, creating a friendly atmosphere that becalms the battlers.
It loves to bask in the sunlight. It uses the leaf on its head to seek out warm places.

153.text: The scent of spices comes from around its neck. Somehow, sniffing it makes you want to fight.
The buds that ring its neck give off a spicy aroma that perks people up.
The scent that wafts from the leaves on its neck causes anyone who smells it to become energetic.
A spicy aroma emanates from around its neck. The aroma acts as a stimulant to restore health.

154.text: The aroma that rises from its petals contains a substance that calms aggressive feelings.
Anyone who stands beside it becomes refreshed, just as if they were relaxing in a sunny forest.
Its breath has the fantastic ability to revive dead plants and flowers.

155.text: It is timid and always curls itself up in a ball. If attacked, it flares up its back for protection.
The fire that spouts from its back burns hottest when it is angry. The flaring flames intimidate foes.
Hails from the Johto region. Though usually curled into a ball due to its timid disposition, it harbors tremendous firepower.
It usually stays hunched over. If it is angry or surprised, it shoots flames out of its back.

156.text: Be careful if it turns its back during battle. It means that it will attack with the fire on its back.
It intimidates foes with intense gusts of flames and superheated air. Its quick nimbleness lets it dodge attacks even while scorching an enemy.
This Pokémon is fully covered by nonflammable fur. It can withstand any kind of fire attack.
It intimidates foes with the heat of its flames. The fire burns more strongly when it readies to fight.

157.text: If its rage peaks, it becomes so hot that anything that touches it will instantly go up in flames.
It attacks using blasts of fire. It creates heat shimmers with intense fire to hide itself.
Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.
It has a secret, devastating move. It rubs its blazing fur together to cause huge explosions.

158.text: Its well-developed jaws are powerful and capable of crushing anything. Even its TRAINER must be careful.
This rough critter chomps at any moving object it sees. Turning your back on it is not recommended.
It is small but rough and tough. It won’t hesitate to take a bite out of anything that moves.
It has the habit of biting anything with its developed jaws. Even its Trainer needs to be careful.

159.text: If it loses a fang, a new one grows back in its place. There are always 48 fangs lining its mouth.
The tips of its fangs are slanted backward. Once those fangs clamp down, the prey has no hope of escape.
Once it bites down, it won’t let go until it loses its fangs. New fangs quickly grow into place.
It opens its huge jaws wide when attacking. If it loses any fangs while biting, they grow back in.

160.text: When it bites with its massive and powerful jaws, it shakes its head and savagely tears its victim up.
It is hard for it to support its own weight out of water, so it gets down on all fours. But it moves fast.
Although it has a massive body, its powerful hind legs enable it to move quickly, even on the ground.
It usually moves slowly, but it goes at blinding speed when it attacks and bites prey.

161.text: A very cautious Pokémon, it raises itself up using its tail to get a better view of its surroundings.
They take turns standing guard when it is time to sleep. The sentry awakens the others if it senses danger. If one becomes separated, it turns sleepless with fear.
It stands on its tail so it can see a long way. If it spots an enemy, it cries loudly to warn its kind.
When acting as a lookout, it warns others of danger by screeching and hitting the ground with its tail.

162.text: It makes a nest to suit its long and skinny body. The nest is impossible for other Pokémon to enter.
There is no telling where its tail begins. Despite its short legs, it is quick at hunting RATTATA.
It lives in narrow burrows that fit its slim body. The deeper the nests go, the more mazelike they become.
The mother puts its offspring to sleep by curling up around them. It corners foes with speed.

163.text: It always stands on one foot. It changes feet so fast, the movement can rarely be seen.
It has a perfect sense of time. Whatever happens, it keeps rhythm by precisely tilting its head in time.
It cries out at the same time every day. A long time ago, people cherished it and considered it a divine messenger sent to tell the time.
It marks time precisely. Some countries consider it to be a wise friend, versed in the world’s ways.

164.text: Its eyes are specially adapted. They concentrate even faint light and enable it to see in the dark.
When it turns its head entirely upside down, you know it’s troubled by something. If you don’t leave it be, it will peck you.
Its extremely soft feathers make no sound in flight. It silently sneaks up on prey without being detected.
When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.

165.text: It is very timid. It will be afraid to move if it is alone. But it will be active if it is in a group.
They communicate with one another using bodily fluids that give off odors. When they’re angry, their odor smells sour.
These very cowardly Pokémon join together and use Reflect to protect their nest.
It is timid and clusters together with others. The fluid secreted by its feet indicates its location.

166.text: When the stars flicker in the night sky, it flutters about, scattering a glowing powder.
In battle, it throws punches with all four arms. The power of each individual blow is piddly, so it aims to win by quantity rather than quality.
While it’s believed that starlight provides it with energy, this Pokémon also loves to eat berries. In the daytime, it curls up in the grass to sleep.
It flies through the night sky, sprinkling sparkly dust. According to some, if that dust sticks to you, good things will happen to you.

167.text: It lies still in the same pose for days in its web, waiting for its unsuspecting prey to wander close.
With threads from its mouth, it fashions sturdy webs that won’t break even if you set a rock on them.
Some fishermen weave its sturdy thread into nets to catch fish Pokémon.
If prey becomes ensnared in its nest of spun string, it waits motionlessly until it becomes dark.

168.text: It spins string not only from its rear but also from its mouth. It is hard to tell which end is which.
Rather than making a nest in one specific spot, it wanders in search of food after darkness falls.
Its feet are tipped with tiny hooked claws that enable it to scuttle on ceilings and vertical walls. It constricts its foe with thin and strong silk webbing.
Every night, it wanders around in search of prey, whose movements it restrains by spewing threads before it bites into them with its fangs.

169.text: It flies so silently through the dark on its four wings that it may not be noticed even when nearby.
As a result of its pursuit of faster, yet more silent flight, a new set of wings grew on its hind legs.
It feeds on the blood of living people and Pokémon. If it can’t drink any blood for even a short while, it becomes weak and unable to fly.
A Pokémon that gained vastly enhanced flying performance by having its legs turn into wings.

170.text: It shoots positive and negative electricity between the tips of its two antennae and zaps its enemies.
On the dark ocean floor, its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights.
Its two antennae glow softly to lure in prey, making it a useful Pokémon for night fishing.
It lives in the depths beyond the reach of sunlight. It flashes lights on its antennae to communicate with others of its kind.

171.text: The light it emits is so bright that it can illuminate the sea’s surface from a depth of over three miles.
It lives far down in the depths of the ocean. It blinds its prey with light, using the moment they’re dazzled to swallow them whole.
This Pokémon uses the bright part of its body, which changed from a dorsal fin, to lure prey.
It blinds prey with an intense burst of light. With the prey incapacitated, the Pokémon swallows it in a single gulp.

172.text: It is not yet skilled at storing electricity. It may send out a jolt if amused or startled.
Despite this Pokémon’s cute appearance, those who want to live with one should prepare to be on the receiving end of its electric jolts.
Despite its small size, it can zap even adult humans. However, if it does so, it also surprises itself.
It still can’t use electricity well. When it’s surprised or excited, it discharges electricity unintentionally.

173.text: Because of its unusual, starlike silhouette, people believe that it came here on a meteor.
Many appear when the night skies are filled with shooting stars. They disappear with sunrise.
If the impact site of a meteorite is found, this Pokémon is certain to be within the immediate area.
On late nights illuminated by shooting stars, it gazes intently skyward, as if thinking of its home.

174.text: It has a very soft body. If it starts to roll, it will bounce all over and be impossible to stop.
It’s always practicing its singing because it wants to improve. Even when it’s asleep, it keeps singing in its dreams!
Instead of walking with its short legs, it moves around by bouncing on its soft, tender body.
It likes to sing but is not yet good at it. With praise and encouragement, it will get better little by little.

175.text: The shell seems to be filled with joy. It is said that it will share good luck when treated kindly.
As its energy, it uses the feelings of compassion and pleasure exuded by people and Pokémon. It stores up happy feelings in its shell, then shares them out.
This ovate creature is frequently mistaken for a moving egg when encountered out in the fields or in the mountains. Its guileless smile soothes the soul.
It transforms the kindness and joy of others into happiness, which it stores in its shell.

176.text: They say that it will appear before kindhearted, caring people and shower them with happiness.
Although it does not flap its wings very much, it can stay up in the air as it tags along after its trainer.
It is said to appear in front of kindly people to scatter a glowing down called “joy dust.”
To share its happiness, it flies around the world seeking kind- hearted people.

177.text: Because its wings aren’t yet fully grown, it has to hop to get around. It is always staring at something.
It picks food from cactus plants, deftly avoiding buds and spines. It seems to skip about to move.
It usually forages for food on the ground but may, on rare occasions, hop onto branches to peck at shoots.
Although it still can’t fly, its jumping power is outstanding. It jumps way up into trees and plucks the buds from the branches.

178.text: They say that it stays still and quiet because it is seeing both the past and future at the same time.
Once it begins to meditate at sunrise, the entire day will pass before it will move again.
It’s said that while this Pokémon has the power to predict the future, it’s not powerful enough to change the future it sees.
While it can see the future, it has no desire to change it, which is probably why it remains motionless at all times.

179.text: If static electricity builds in its body, its fleece doubles in volume. Touching it will shock you.
Its fluffy wool rubs together and builds a static charge. The more energy is charged, the more brightly the lightbulb at the tip of its tail glows.
It stores lots of air in its soft fur, allowing it to stay cool in summer and warm in winter.
Its fleece grows continually. In the summer, the fleece is fully shed, but it grows back in a week.

180.text: As a result of storing too much electricity, it developed patches where even downy wool won’t grow.
If its coat becomes fully charged with electricity, its tail lights up. It fires hair that zaps on impact.
Its fluffy fleece easily stores electricity. Its rubbery hide keeps it from being electrocuted.
Its fleece quality changes to generate strong static electricity with a small amount of wool. The bare, slick parts of its hide are shielded against electricity.

181.text: The tail’s tip shines brightly and can be seen from far away. It acts as a beacon for lost people.
The light from its tail can be seen from space. This is why you can always tell exactly where it is, which is why it usually keeps the light off.
The tip of its tail shines brightly. In the olden days, people sent signals using the tail’s light.
The tip of its tail shines so brightly it can be used to send sea-navigation beacons to distant foreign shores.

182.text: Plentiful in the tropics. When it dances, its petals rub together and make a pleasant ringing sound.
When the heavy rainfall season ends, it is drawn out by warm sunlight to dance in the open.
When these dance together, their petals rub against each other, making pretty, relaxing sounds.
Its flower petals deepen in color through exposure to sunlight. When cloudy weather persists, it does a dance that is thought to be a ritual for summoning the sun.

183.text: The tip of its tail, which contains oil that is lighter than water, lets it swim without drowning.
The oil-filled tail functions as a buoy, so it’s fine even in rivers with strong currents.
Using its tail as a float, it dives underwater. It likes eating plants that grow on river bottoms.
The fur on its body naturally repels water. It can stay dry, even when it plays in the water.

184.text: By keeping still and listening intently, it can tell what is in even wild, fast-moving rivers.
When it plays in water, it rolls up its elongated ears to prevent their insides from getting wet.
Its long ears are superb sensors. It can distinguish the movements of living things on riverbeds.
It can spend all day in water, since it can inhale and store a large volume of air.

185.text: Although it always pretends to be a tree, its composition appears to be closer to a rock than a plant.
The result of its holding the same pose all the time is arms that have become supple yet strong.
Apparently, the larger the green parts of this Pokémon, the more collectors value it. It’s a particular favorite among elderly people.
